_comment_family: The one face in this folder whose file gets its own family name wrong,
and the reason this pack has to be read before the name is touched.
The four names in the file disagree: the family (name ID 1) says
'Mongoose Regular', the subfamily (ID 2) says 'Bold', the full name
(ID 4) says 'Mongoose Bold' and the PostScript name (ID 6) says
'Mongoose-Bold'. Only ID 1 is wrong, and it is wrong in the worst
direction: it names a cut this file is not, so a machine that went
looking by family would be told this is the Regular.
None of that reaches the app, because a pack-declared face is
registered with the browser under the name stated HERE, against the
url below (see registerFace in js/channels.js). The family in this
file is a label the app chooses for a file it already has, not a
question it asks the machine. 'Mongoose Bold' is therefore both true
and safe to declare, and it is what the rest of the pack is written
against.
Where the file's names DO matter is `local` below, which is the one
route that asks the machine for a face by name - and that list is
written out of ID 4 and ID 6 for exactly this reason. 'Mongoose' alone
is deliberately absent, the way 'Telegraf' is absent from the two
Telegraf packs: it is a family name with cuts under it, and a machine
with the Regular installed would answer with a face at half this
weight. 'Mongoose Regular' is absent for the stronger version of the
same reason - it is the name this file gives its family, and it names
the wrong cut.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass, what the subfamily
calls it, and what the bold bit in fsSelection says.

_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file:
the Windows full name (ID 4) first, the PostScript name (ID 6) behind
it. Both name this one cut rather than the family it sits in - see the
note above, which is the whole of why this list is two names and not
The first is also the name the installer registers the face under. It
copies each pack's font into the user's font folder and keys it by
local[0] (see engine.install_fonts), and Windows keys installed fonts
by their full name, so the installed copy lands under the same name
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice, and on
this face they are barely even that. Mongoose Bold is an ultra
condensed: its capitals average 0.300em - an O at 0.296, an M at 0.478
- which is under half the 0.620em of the New Order Medium it picks
words out of. Twenty capitals at the Snapchat preset's 40px come out
at 240px of a 486px line.
Nothing a Windows machine can be relied on to have is within reach of
that. The same twenty capitals measure: Impact 407px, Segoe UI Bold
526px, Arial Bold 550px, Arial Black 615px. The nearest of them is 70%
wider than the face, which is not a substitution anybody would ship -
it is the difference between a picked word that is half the width of
its neighbours and one that is wider than them.
So the order below is nearest-first among faces that exist, and it is
written knowing it cannot save the layout. What actually protects this
channel is fontguard, which verifies BOTH of a two-face channel's
faces before anything is measured and names the missing one in the
banner rather than drawing with a stand-in (see js/fontguard.js and
`highlight.face` in js/channels.js). This stack is what a browser
reaches for in the seconds before that check answers, and Impact is
the least wrong thing to reach for: a heavy condensed grotesque is at
least the same KIND of face, where the Segoe UI and Arial behind it
are only a promise that something will be drawn.
Arial Black is absent, as it is everywhere else in this folder. At
157% over it is not a fallback, it is a guarantee of overflow.
